summary: Multiplexed SSE sessions + proxy cookie rotation splits/duplicates final sentence on resume
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that during high-concurrency usage behind a corporate proxy which rewrites cookies, SSE streaming sessions sometimes end with the last sentence split across two resumed fragments or duplicated. Impact: generated output is split mid-sentence or contains a duplicated trailing clause, which breaks downstream parsers and leads to user-visible corruption in final responses. Occurs on multiplexed sessions when the client reconnects and the proxy rotates cookies mid-session.
impact: Some customer requests return corrupted final sentence (either truncated, duplicated tail, or split across resume boundary). Affects enterprise customers behind proxies that rewrite Set-Cookie (OmniDocs reported ~1 in 1k resume events degraded). Business impact: customer-facing document generation pipelines get malformed outputs and some automated QA rejects outputs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a multiplexed SSE session with multiple concurrent stream IDs to the Redwood hosted API.
2) Place the client behind a proxy that rewrites or rotates cookies on short TTLs (simulate corporate proxy behavior).
3) Start a long-form generation (sequence > 600 tokens) which streams via SSE.
4) Force a reconnect mid-generation by simulating a TCP reconnect or proxy cookie swap.
5) Observe resume behavior: some resumed streams present duplicated trailing clauses or the final sentence split across resume fragments and missing closing punctuation.

2026-03-10T09:12:34Z - customer-client: received fragment N (partial sentence), then received a resumed fragment with overlapping tokens -> observed duplicated tail and split sentence
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Confirmed reproduction with customer's proxy simulator. Hypothesis: cookie rotation causes api-gateway to rebind multiplexed session to different internal routing identity, causing resume_token routing mismatch.
SRE reproduced locally by injecting Set-Cookie rotation in frontproxy; observed routing change at api-gateway layer when cookie changed mid-resume.

Worker-level logs show that worker handling the resumed connection lacked the primed KV cache for that session seq and triggered resend of trailing buffer which overlaps with previously-acknowledged tokens, producing duplicated tails.

Resume handler currently trusts resume_token that uses both session_id and cookie-derived affinity; when cookie changes, resume_token resolves to different worker without reconciling outstanding fragments.
hypothesis: Cookie-based affinity rotation during multiplexed SSE resumes can map the same resume_token to a different routing identity. The new worker doesn't have identical in-memory tail buffer/kv-state, so it replays or emits buffered trailing tokens; client merges resulting fragments and sees duplicate or split final sentence.
workarounds_proposed: 1) Customer: configure corporate proxy to preserve cookie TTL for streaming endpoints or disable cookie rewriting for *.redwood.ai endpoints.
2) Client: on resume, prefer authorization headers (Bearer) or resume token in query param instead of relying on cookies for affinity.
3) Support: temporarily route customer to dedicated capacity where session affinity is stable (Dedicated).

2026-03-11 - Eng (Diego): instrumented resume handler to log resolved affinity identity and resume_token mapping for affected sessions.
2026-03-12 - SRE: rolled a canary patch to gate resume routing by session_id primary key (ignore cookie-derived fallback) for multiplexed SSE resumes in canary region us-east.
2026-03-13 - Eng: prepared follow-up patch to attach a small per-session durable resume buffer persisted to ephemeral storage for brief handoffs (PR linked).
resolution_notes: Mitigations: canary routing change (route by persistent session_id first, cookie affinity second) reduced duplication rate from ~0.1% to <0.001% in canary. Long-term fix: implement authoritative resume-ownership lookup that reconciles session resume_token with a durable minimal resume buffer so workers can hand off mid-resume without replaying overlapping fragments. Patch PR created and under review: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1843. Customer agreed to temporary proxy change pending rollout.
resolution_status: Partial workaround in place; code fix under review and scheduled for next minor release.
